findings.body: The page begins with stage counts followed by the dependency map. It has no plain-English summary naming what is moving, what is waiting and its blockers, stalled items and their idle durations, the part blocking the most others, or the stage consuming the most recorded time. The renderer in board.py:907–915 supplies only counts, map and existing sections; none computes these required bottleneck lines. Add the requested summary above the map, deriving it from the shared command data and preserving unknown values.
findings.title: Not done: Designed for a project manager who opens the page cold, solo or with a team, and must see within seconds what is happening

findings.body: An approved story is assigned "building" here, and no subsequent path assigns it "ready to merge", even when its only remaining part has a valid close receipt and forge next reports that part ready to merge. board.py:449–460 consumes this value directly, so the summary incorrectly reports Building: 1 and Ready to merge: 0 for that story. The positive readiness test at tests/test_board_dependency_timelines.py:242–257 exercises only a fix. This finding preserves the ruling to count each story once; the new evidence is that the story-stage producer never emits the ready-to-merge stage. Derive that stage from the remaining parts' readiness and cover the story case through the command.
findings.title: Not done: include merge-ready stories in the stage totals

findings.body: Neither parametrized client case checks the required top summary or its bottleneck lines. The page assertions check maps, timelines, existing sections and counts, but never assert a stalled item's duration, the largest blocking part, or the stage where most time goes. Consequently, the supplied nine-test run passes with the entire required summary absent. Extend the real board-command test for both new and earlier-adopted clients with deterministic summary data and assertions above the roadmap.
findings.title: Not done: test_dependency_map_and_stage_timelines_use_the_command_data

findings.body: The complete latest proof list omits an entry covering the required impeccable shaping, audit and polish pass with emil-design-eng's checklist. Its visual-proof entry names SVG metadata, palette tokens and responsive CSS checks, which do not document that required design pass. The coordinator's ruling permits command-rendered SVG/CSS proof and defers live browser checking; this finding does not request browser tooling. Add a verifiable entry for the required skill work and checking pass.
findings.title: Not done: proof list
